passages.text: Bel crouches; Nebo cowers. Their idols weigh down beasts and cattle. The images you carry are burdensome, a load to the weary animal.
passages.sermon:
Bel is a false god.
Bel crouches down.
Nebo is a false god.
Nebo cowers.
People make idols of Bel and Nebo.
These idols are heavy.
The idols weigh down animals.
The idols weigh down cattle.
People carry these images.
The images are a burden.
The burden is heavy for tired animals.
passages.original: כָּרַ֥ע בֵּל֙ קֹרֵ֣ס נְב֔וֹ הָיוּ֙ עֲצַבֵּיהֶ֔ם לַחַיָּ֖ה וְלַבְּהֵמָ֑ה נְשֻׂאֹתֵיכֶ֣ם עֲמוּס֔וֹת מַשָּׂ֖א לַעֲיֵפָֽה׃

passages.text: The gods cower; they crouch together, unable to relieve the burden; but they themselves go into captivity.
passages.sermon:
The false gods cower.
They crouch together.
They cannot lift the burden.
They cannot save anyone from the load.
These gods go into captivity themselves.
passages.original: קָרְס֤וּ כָֽרְעוּ֙ יַחְדָּ֔ו לֹ֥א יָכְל֖וּ מַלֵּ֣ט מַשָּׂ֑א וְנַפְשָׁ֖ם בַּשְּׁבִ֥י הָלָֽכָה׃ס

passages.text: “Listen to Me, O house of Jacob, all the remnant of the house of Israel, who have been sustained from the womb, carried along since birth.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the house of Jacob.
God speaks to all who remain from the house of Israel.
God has carried you since you were in the womb.
God has supported you since you were born.
passages.original: שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ בֵּ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְכָל־ שְׁאֵרִ֖ית בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הַֽעֲמֻסִים֙ מִנִּי־ בֶ֔טֶן הַנְּשֻׂאִ֖ים מִנִּי־ רָֽחַם׃

passages.text: Even to your old age, I will be the same, and I will bear you up when you turn gray. I have made you, and I will carry you; I will sustain you and deliver you.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the house of Jacob and the remnant of Israel.
God says, “I am always the same.”
God says, “I will be with you even when you are old.”
God says, “I will carry you when your hair turns gray.”
God says, “I made you.”
God says, “I will carry you.”
God says, “I will support you.”
God says, “I will rescue you.”
passages.original: וְעַד־ זִקְנָה֙ אֲנִ֣י ה֔וּא וְעַד־ שֵיבָ֖ה אֲנִ֣י אֶסְבֹּ֑ל אֲנִ֤י עָשִׂ֙יתִי֙ וַאֲנִ֣י אֶשָּׂ֔א וַאֲנִ֥י אֶסְבֹּ֖ל וַאֲמַלֵּֽט׃ס

passages.text: To whom will you liken Me or count Me equal? To whom will you compare Me, that we should be alike?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God asks a question.
God says, “Who is like Me?”
God says, “Who is equal to Me?”
God says, “Who can you compare to Me?”
God says, “Who is the same as I am?”

passages.text: They pour out their bags of gold and weigh out silver on scales; they hire a goldsmith to fashion it into a god, so they can bow down and worship.
passages.sermon:
People take gold from their bags.
They weigh silver on scales.
They hire a goldsmith.
The goldsmith makes the gold and silver into a god.
They bow down to this god.
They worship this god.
passages.original: הַזָּלִ֤ים זָהָב֙ מִכִּ֔יס וְכֶ֖סֶף בַּקָּנֶ֣ה יִשְׁקֹ֑לוּ יִשְׂכְּר֤וּ צוֹרֵף֙ וְיַעֲשֵׂ֣הוּ אֵ֔ל יִסְגְּד֖וּ אַף־ יִֽשְׁתַּחֲוּֽוּ׃

passages.text: They lift it to their shoulder and carry it along; they set it in its place, and there it stands, not budging from that spot. They cry out to it, but it does not answer; it saves no one from his troubles.
passages.sermon:
People make idols from gold and silver.
They lift the idol onto their shoulder.
They carry the idol as they walk.
They set the idol down in its place.
The idol stands there and does not move.
The idol cannot leave its spot.
People cry out to the idol.
The idol does not answer them.
The idol cannot save anyone from trouble.
passages.original: יִ֠שָּׂאֻהוּ עַל־ כָּתֵ֨ף יִסְבְּלֻ֜הוּ וְיַנִּיחֻ֤הוּ תַחְתָּיו֙ וְיַֽעֲמֹ֔ד מִמְּקוֹמ֖וֹ לֹ֣א יָמִ֑ישׁ אַף־ יִצְעַ֤ק אֵלָיו֙ וְלֹ֣א יַעֲנֶ֔ה מִצָּרָת֖וֹ לֹ֥א יוֹשִׁיעֶֽנּוּ׃ס

passages.text: Remember this and be brave; take it to heart, you transgressors!
passages.sermon:
God speaks to people who have sinned.
He tells them to remember what He says.
He commands them to be strong and brave.
He tells them to take His words seriously.
He calls them transgressors.
He urges them to think deeply about His warning.
passages.original: זִכְרוּ־ זֹ֖את וְהִתְאֹשָׁ֑שׁוּ הָשִׁ֥יבוּ פוֹשְׁעִ֖ים עַל־ לֵֽב׃

passages.text: Remember what happened long ago, for I am God, and there is no other; I am God, and there is none like Me.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people.
God tells them to remember what happened long ago.
God says, "I am God."
There is no other God besides Me.
No one is like Me.
passages.original: זִכְר֥וּ רִאשֹׁנ֖וֹת מֵעוֹלָ֑ם כִּ֣י אָנֹכִ֥י אֵל֙ וְאֵ֣ין ע֔וֹד אֱלֹהִ֖ים וְאֶ֥פֶס כָּמֽוֹנִי׃

passages.text: I declare the end from the beginning, and ancient times from what is still to come. I say, ‘My purpose will stand, and all My good pleasure I will accomplish.’
passages.sermon:
God speaks in this passage.
God is unique.
God is not like anyone else.
God declares what will happen at the end.
God declares this from the very beginning.
God tells about things from ancient times.
God tells about things that have not happened yet.
God says, "My purpose will stand."
God says, "I will do everything I desire."
passages.original: מַגִּ֤יד מֵֽרֵאשִׁית֙ אַחֲרִ֔ית וּמִקֶּ֖דֶם אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־ נַעֲשׂ֑וּ אֹמֵר֙ עֲצָתִ֣י תָק֔וּם וְכָל־ חֶפְצִ֖י אֶעֱשֶֽׂה׃

passages.text: I summon a bird of prey from the east, a man for My purpose from a far-off land. Truly I have spoken, and truly I will bring it to pass. I have planned it, and I will surely do it.
passages.sermon:
God speaks these words.
God has all power and authority.
God calls a bird of prey from the east.
God summons a man from a distant land for His purpose.
God has spoken these things.
God will make them happen.
God has planned this.
God will surely do it.
passages.original: קֹרֵ֤א מִמִּזְרָח֙ עַ֔יִט מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מֶרְחָ֖ק אִ֣ישׁ עֲצָתוֹ אַף־ דִּבַּ֙רְתִּי֙ אַף־ אֲבִיאֶ֔נָּה יָצַ֖רְתִּי אַף־ אֶעֱשֶֽׂנָּה׃ס

passages.text: Listen to Me, you stubborn people, far removed from righteousness: I am bringing My righteousness near; it is not far away, and My salvation will not be delayed. I will grant salvation to Zion and adorn Israel with My splendor.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to stubborn people.
These people are far from righteousness.
God says, "Listen to Me."
I am bringing My righteousness close.
My righteousness is not far away.
My salvation will not be delayed.
I will give salvation to Zion.
I will give Israel My splendor.
passages.original: שִׁמְע֥וּ אֵלַ֖י אַבִּ֣ירֵי לֵ֑ב הָרְחוֹקִ֖ים מִצְּדָקָֽה׃ קֵרַ֤בְתִּי צִדְקָתִי֙ לֹ֣א תִרְחָ֔ק וּתְשׁוּעָתִ֖י לֹ֣א תְאַחֵ֑ר וְנָתַתִּ֤י בְצִיּוֹן֙ תְּשׁוּעָ֔ה לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל תִּפְאַרְתִּֽי׃ס
